questions.answer: Rēx exsul senātōrēs ōrat ut rēgnum vetus sibi reddant.

questions.prompt: The dying father persuades his sons to preserve the ancestral estate.
questions.answer: Pater moriēns fīliīs persuādet ut fundum avītum cōnservent.

questions.prompt: I do not doubt that the proconsul will restore peace to the province.
questions.answer: Nōn dubitō quīn prōcōnsul pācem prōvinciae restitūtūrus sit.

questions.prompt: We did not doubt that the fleet would soon return into the harbor.
questions.answer: Nōn dubitābāmus quīn classis mox in portum reditūra esset.

questions.prompt: No one doubts that the orator will speak most eloquently before the people.
questions.answer: Nēmō dubitat quīn ōrātor apud populum ēloquentissimē dictūrus sit.

questions.prompt: The king did not doubt that his allies would betray him in the war.
questions.answer: Rēx nōn dubitābat quīn sociī sē in bellō prōditūrī essent.

questions.prompt: The farmer fears that a sudden frost may ruin the tender vines.
questions.answer: Agricola timet nē subita pruīna tenerās vītēs corrumpat.

questions.prompt: The sailors were afraid that the pirates would seize the merchant ship.
questions.answer: Nautae timēbant nē praedōnēs nāvem onerāriam caperent.

questions.prompt: The mother is afraid that her son will not return from the war.
questions.answer: Māter metuit nē fīlius ex bellō nōn redeat.

questions.prompt: The consul feared that the wavering allies would abandon the alliance.
questions.answer: Cōnsul verēbātur nē sociī dubiī societātem dēsererent.

questions.prompt: So great a plague fell upon the city that thousands of citizens perished.
questions.answer: Tanta pestis in urbem incidit ut mīlia cīvium periērint.

questions.prompt: The orator spoke so vehemently that he moved the whole assembly to tears.
questions.answer: Ōrātor tam vehementer dīxit ut tōtam cōntiōnem ad lacrimās mōverit.

questions.prompt: The tyrant so oppressed the people that no one dared to speak freely.
questions.answer: Tyrannus populum ita oppressit ut nēmō līberē loquī audēret.

questions.prompt: The general so fortified the camp that the enemy could not storm it.
questions.answer: Dux castra ita mūnīvit ut ea hostēs expugnāre nōn possent.

questions.prompt: The Gauls promise that they will do whatever the leader commands.
questions.answer: Gallī pollicentur sē factūrōs esse quaecumque dux imperet.

questions.prompt: The soldiers promised that they would follow wherever the commander should lead.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs pollicitī sunt sē secūtūrōs esse quōcumque imperātor dūceret.

questions.prompt: Caesar was waiting to see how large a force the enemy would gather.
questions.answer: Caesar exspectābat quantās cōpiās hostēs cōgerent.

questions.prompt: The envoys promised that they would report whatever the king should have decided.
questions.answer: Lēgātī pollicitī sunt sē nūntiātūrōs esse quaecumque rēx statuisset.
